usage: Said to get a stranger's attention, to squeeze past someone, or to apologise for a small slip. It is polite and neutral, so it works with anyone. The same word is also the standard reply to "thank you", where it means "you're welcome".

variants.label: more formal
variants.note: Use in formal settings or when interrupting someone senior.

variants.label: to a man, to ask for something
variants.note: Use to call a waiter or ask a man for a favour.

variants.label: to a woman, to ask for something
variants.note: The same request addressed to a woman.

variants.label: apologising
variants.note: Use when you have actually got in the way or made a mistake.

examples.english: Excuse me, where is the station?
Excuse me, is this seat free?
Sorry, I did not hear you well.
